newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mixed, pork bellies off on technicals.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mixed, pork bellies off on technicals.

text.p: CME hog futures ended mixed as late profit taking and spread action cut early gains and pork belly futures tumbled as much as the daily limit in the closing range as local selling hit technical sell stops, traders said.

Hog futures ended 0.150 cent lower to 0.275 higher with October up 0.025 at 53.800 cents per lb. February bellies posted a limit loss of 2.000 cents in the closing range but settled 1.925 lower with other months 1.475 to 0.925 lower.
Hog futures were strong much of the day on firm cash but slipped late as demand waned.

Rolling of longs into December pressured October and offset early support from higher cash markets. Anticipation of Goldman Sachs doing their "Goldman roll", moving October longs into December, had little influence on the market early, but was more notable late as trading activity became lighter. However, December also eased late as a few local sell orders met little buying interest, they said.
Expectations of steady to firm cash hog markets Tuesday lent early support, but buying interest eased as futures aleady hold a premium to cash, they added.

Rand Financials, Refco and R.J. O'Brien bought October early before selling by Cargill Investor Services weighed on prices, traders said, adding that RBH sold late. Rand Financials sold December early while LIT division of First Options, Stone Traders and Rosenthal Collins bought, pit sources said.
In hog options, there was general buying of October 52 puts and calls. Rosenthal Collins sold December 57 calls and there was offering of February puts, traders added.
Pork belly futures retreated after showing initial carryover strength and tumbled late as local long liquidation touched off technical sell stops, traders said.
Chartists noted that the rebound in futures last week was overdone and futures were now continuing their downward trend of the previous few weeks.
The market was also pressured by concern over expected increased hog slaughter rates. The hurricane cut hog kills last week but slaughter rates should rebound, they said.

"A lot of people think that there are a few hogs that didn't get killed last week and they will start to catch up as the week progresses," said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp.
